title: Clariflocculator

introduction.definition: A clariflocculator combines flocculation and clarification in one circular tank. Coagulated raw water rises into a central flocculation compartment where slow paddles let tiny particles collide and grow into flocs. The water passes under the compartment skirt into the outer clarifier zone, where flocs settle to the floor and are raked to a central sludge pit, while clear water overflows the peripheral weir.
applications: Surface-water treatment for drinking and process water
Clarification of cooling-tower make-up and industrial raw water
key_points: Coagulate → flocculate → settle in one unit
Low surface loading (≈ 1–2 m/h) lets flocs settle
Rakes move sludge to the central pit

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

video_tutorials.title: Clariflocculator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Clariflocculator.
Check effluent turbidity, sludge blanket level and rake torque.
Clean weirs/launders (algae); check paddle bearings.
Drain, inspect rakes, scrapers and drive gear; repair concrete.
Watch for floc carry-over: high outlet turbidity. Common cause: overloading.
Watch for rake overload trip: torque alarm, drive stops. Common cause: heavy sludge accumulation.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
